caption: The video captures a high aerial view of a wind farm rising above a thick, rolling sea of low cloud under a grey overcast sky. A large three-blade turbine dominates the right foreground, its white tower running down to the bottom edge. The rotor of this foreground turbine turns continuously. Its blades sweep steadily around the hub in a clockwise sense. Two smaller turbines stand in the middle ground within a gap of green ground, and their rotors also show changing blade orientations, indicating they are turning as well. A faint row of additional turbines lines the left horizon above the cloud layer, remaining small. The cloud and fog surface drifts and reshapes slowly, with the bright green ground patches and dark gaps between the turbines shifting in shape and extent over time. The overall framing of the turbines and the horizon stays essentially fixed, so the visible motion comes mainly from the rotating blades and the moving fog. The rotors keep spinning and the fog keeps swirling, an ongoing process rather than a completed action.
relations: If the foreground rotor turns, its blades sweep clockwise around the fixed hub.
The middle-ground turbine hubs stay fixed while their blade orientations change as rotors turn.
The low cloud surface drifts, altering visible gaps and green ground patches over time.
The aerial framing remains steady, keeping turbine positions and horizon fixed as motion occurs.
